title: LiveWorld — Turn a tabletop into a testable world
disclosures: Edited capture of the actual application
Recorded Meta playtests are labelled as replays

scenes.heading: Your desk becomes a testable world
scenes.caption: AI-generated input · roles are reviewed by the creator
scenes.narration: LiveWorld turns a tabletop into a game-system experiment. This demo uses clearly labelled, AI-generated images: a cup is a water source, blocks are homes, and two wooden sticks become bridges.

scenes.heading: Muse Spark sees meaning. SAM traces shape.
scenes.caption: Actual Meta response · model waiting time omitted
scenes.narration: Muse Spark locates the objects and suggests their roles. SAM traces their shapes. These are actual returned masks, not hand-drawn overlays. The creator reviews every role before any object enters the simulation.

scenes.heading: A simulation with rules, not invented outcomes
scenes.caption: Movement, water accounting, queues and deadlines run in code
scenes.narration: After confirmation, image-relative positions map to a fixed grid. Couriers move, water is produced, and each household has a deadline. The simulator computes every delivery and queue; the model does not invent the outcome.

scenes.heading: One bridge moves. Measure what changes.
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta captures · waiting 22 → 10 · on time remains 20/24
scenes.narration: Here is a replay of two actual Meta captures. Only the lower bridge changes grid position. Waiting drops from twenty-two to ten turns, but on-time delivery remains twenty out of twenty-four. A useful change is not automatically a solved level.

scenes.heading: Give the playtester a constrained problem
scenes.caption: Authored valley example · six couriers · baseline 20/24 on time
scenes.narration: Now switch to an authored level: six couriers, twenty-four units, fixed household deadlines. Twenty arrive on time. This recording replays a real Meta playtest, with every result recalculated.

scenes.heading: A plausible proposal can fail
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta trial · balanced dispatch delivers only 14/24 on time
scenes.narration: The agent's balanced-dispatch proposal looks plausible, but only fourteen units arrive on time. Code marks the trial as unsuccessful. A model's confident explanation cannot turn a failed experiment into a successful one.

scenes.heading: The world has the final say
scenes.caption: Recorded Meta trial · 24/24 on time · waiting 16 → 22 turns
scenes.narration: Moving the south bridge is a verified fix: all twenty-four units arrive on time, with the original six couriers, demand and deadlines. Waiting increases from sixteen to twenty-two turns, so that trade-off stays visible. Success is checked independently by the simulator.

scenes.heading: Design rules in plain language
scenes.caption: Creator instruction · separate from the same-resource agent challenge
scenes.narration: Creators can also change the game itself. Here the instruction asks Muse Spark to use eight couriers while keeping every other rule unchanged.

scenes.heading: Review the exact change before applying
scenes.caption: Live Meta rule proposal · couriers 6 → 8 · outcome recomputed
scenes.narration: The instruction becomes a validated proposal. Only couriers change from six to eight. This creator design change is clearly separated from a same-resource playtest fix.

scenes.heading: Keep a branch. Keep the original.
scenes.caption: Apply B · original A is retained as a checkpoint
scenes.narration: Apply the candidate to keep designing. LiveWorld saves the original as a checkpoint. You can compare against it later, change your mind, or branch from a different layout.

scenes.heading: Save it. Open it. Recompute it.
scenes.caption: Portable project · layouts, photos, checkpoints and verified trials
scenes.narration: Save the whole project, including photos, checkpoints and trials. Reopening it validates the inputs and recalculates the measurements, instead of trusting a saved success flag.

scenes.heading: Build a world. Find what breaks. Test the fix.
scenes.caption: Built by Tang Vu · powered by Meta · github.com/tang-vu/liveworld
scenes.narration: Export inspectable evidence. LiveWorld helps game creators test fixed-camera tabletop layouts through deterministic, replayable experiments.
